title: Patch window orchestration log and smoke matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the orchestration log, calendar, and an actionable smoke-test matrix for the June patch window (candidate patch: service-mux v1.14.2). Intended audience: release lead, SRE on-call, infra, backend owners, and product ops.

High-level objectives:
- Apply security backport + small routing fix with minimal user impact.
- Ensure we can detect and rapidly mitigate regressions with a 20-minute mean time to mitigation target.
- Validate telemetry and sampling so post-patch signal analysis is meaningful.

Patch window summary:
- Window start: 2026-06-09 22:00 UTC (preflight checks begin at 21:00 UTC)
- Expected diameter: 45 minutes for rolling patch, 2 hours full stabilization window
- Impact domain: serving-runtime API tier (primary), no DB schema changes, no migrations
- Risk class: Medium

Roles and contact list (primary then backup):
- Release lead: Marcus Chen (pager: +1-555-0143) / backup: Aisha Patel
- SRE on-call: Nina Park / backup: Samuel Ortiz
- Infra lead (GPU infra): Diego Alvarez / backup: Priya Rao
- Routing/edge: Benji Carter / backup: Devika Singh
- PM escalation: Lucia Wong

Preflight checklist (T-60 to T-0):
- T-60: Verify canary image signed and stored (artifact url) - Marcus
- T-50: Confirm capacity reservations in Dedicated pools for canary traffic - Diego
- T-45: Smoke harness dry run in staging (same seed traffic) - Nina
- T-40: Telemetry retention bump for 2 hours post-patch (debug traces ON) - Aisha
- T-30: Postmortem PO assigned and doc stub created - Marcus
- T-20: Notify CS/GTM channel with downtime expectations and contact matrix - Lucia
- T-10: Ensure rollback image is pre-tagged and pre-validated - Diego
- T-05: Open release signal board, set alert escalations and paging routes - Nina
- T-00: Start rolling canary (10% of traffic) - Release lead triggers

Rolling plan and calendar (minute-granular):
- 22:00 UTC: Start canary deployment (10% weight) -> 5 minutes for deploy + 10 for warm-up
- 22:15 UTC: Run smoke matrix against canary endpoints (see matrix below)
- 22:25 UTC: If pass, promote to 50% (phased across regions: us-west, eu-west)
- 22:45 UTC: 50% smoke run and light load soak (30s QPS spike test)
- 23:05 UTC: Promote to 100% (if both regional soaks OK)
- 23:10-00:30 UTC: Stabilization monitoring window, sampling 1/50 requests for traces
- 00:30 UTC: Final sign-off and close window unless rollback triggered

Smoke-test matrix (quick checks to run against each canary cohort):
Columns: Check, Endpoint, Expected, Run-method, Owner, Fail-action
1) Health and readiness: GET /health -> 200 + healthy=true -> curl + json check -> Nina -> rollback if >5% failures
2) Basic generation latency: POST /v1/generate small prompt -> median < 110ms -> scripted harness -> Backend owner (Benji) -> rollback if median >200ms for 3 min
3) KV cache hit sanity: POST cached prefix -> hit ratio delta < 5% -> synthetic prefetched keys -> Diego -> pause rollout and investigate cache warming
4) Token-stream correctness: small streaming session -> no truncated frames, tokens in order -> e2e script -> Marcus -> rollback if any truncations detected
5) Auth & rate-limit: high concurrency auth check -> no 401 spikes and rate-limit headers intact -> stress harness -> DevOps -> rollback if >1% 401 increase
6) Telemetry integrity: sample traces appear with new image tag metadata -> telemetry query -> Aisha -> abort and revert if traces missing for >2 min
7) Error budget smoke: alerting trigger simulation -> SLO alert not firing unexpectedly -> manual check -> SRE -> rollback if false-positive alerts >2 triggers

Failure and rollback matrix (failure type -> immediate action -> owner):
- Crash loops / process OOM -> Stop rollout, scale down new pods, revert to prev image -> Infra lead (Diego)
- Latency regression across 3 regions -> Pause promotion, route traffic away from affected region, start canary rollback -> SRE + Release lead
- Incorrect responses / malformed streaming -> Immediate full rollback and page Backend owner; open incident bridge -> Marcus + Benji
- Missing telemetry / traces -> Pause acceptance, do an exp run with debug ON; if unresolved in 15m revert -> Aisha

Operator runbook snippets (commands / checks):
- Promote cohort: kubectl set image deploy/serving-runtime serving-runtime=registry/redwood/serving-runtime:v1.14.2-canary --record
- Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deploy/serving-runtime --to-revision=Previous && kubectl rollout status deploy/serving-runtime
- Quick health: curl -sS https://serving-api.prod/health | jq .status
- Check trace presence: curl "https://telemetry.redwood/api/trace?q=tag:build=v1.14.2" | head

Telemetry and sampling notes:
- For 60 minutes after full rollout, increase trace sampling to 1/50 (default 1/500) and store high-resolution latencies for 2 hours
- Emit a synthetic trace on every canary promotion event with fields: image_tag, cohort_id, region, deploy_ts
- Ensure alerting runbooks are pinned in the signal board with runbook links and on-call steps

Post-patch verification (T+0 to T+120m):
- T+5: Confirm error rate stable and any new 5xx traces are <0.1% of traffic
- T+15: Check median P95 latency across regions and compare to baseline runbook
- T+30: Validate KV cache warming by comparing point-in-time hit ratios to baseline (expect +/- 3%)
- T+60: Review sampled traces for integrity and instrumented metadata
- T+120: Draft preliminary post-patch note and attach top 3 anomalies to the release doc

Notes for the release notes draft (internal -> external separation):
- Internal: list of fixed tickets, mitigations, profiling notes, side-effects (e.g., increased debug logging for 2 hours), rollback procedures used if any
- External (customer-facing): brief description of the change (security backport + routing fix), expected improvements, no customer action required, and link to status page if degraded.

Known open issues to watch during window:
- INFRA-1234: intermittent NVLink flakiness on g4-pools at night — mitigation: ensure canary allocation avoids those nodes
- RELEASE-482: edge routing TTL mismatch under heavy tail traffic — limited to 0.01% of requests but monitor for drift

Quick after-action template (to fill within 24h):
- Summary (one-liner)
- Timeline (actions taken with timestamps)
- What went well
- What failed / anomalies with metric snapshots
- Root cause (if applicable) and next steps
- Owners for follow-up tasks and ETA

Appendix: artifacts and checkpoints
- Candidate image: registry/redwood/serving-runtime:v1.14.2-canary
- Rollback image: registry/redwood/serving-runtime:v1.14.1-stable
- Staging smoke harness job: ci/staging/smoke/serving-runtime (build 4521)
note: Draft. Keep this doc as the single source-of-truth for the June patch window orchestration. Update live during the window and link incident notes as they are created.
